messages:
alex_m: Heads-up — we saw a persistent imbalance on the runtime where lots of small (<=32 token) requests are pushing long-running streams (>512 tokens) into huge latency tails. p95 for short requests ok, but p99 for long ones jumped 3-4x after yesterday's kernel selector tweak.
meera: Can you paste the profiling snippet? curious if it's batching or kernel churn.
alex_m: quick snippet from the profiler (aggregated across 3x A100 pools):
```
batch_size_distribution: {short: 68%, med: 22%, long: 10%}
avg_batch_latency_ms: {short: 18, med: 42, long: 230}
kv_cache_hit_by_len: {short: 0.72, long: 0.39}
kernel_switches_per_seq: {short: 1.1, long: 3.7}
```
sam_s: hmm kernel_switches_per_seq for long sequences looks terrifying — likely the new kernel selection path is fragmenting long runs into many small kernel invocations. that increases scheduling and causes KV thrash.
jin: Agree. Also suspect batching policy is greedily filling batches with short requests, then when a long seq arrives it gets stuck waiting for its own tokens to be serviced. We should try age-based weighting for batch admission (give older/long sequences priority for next batch).
katie: Can we quantify fairness? propose metric: normalized latency delta = p99_long / p99_short over time, and tail-fairness (fraction of long seqs in top 1% latency). I put a quick dashboard link in #eng-runtime-dash (placeholder). :link:
alex_m: Proposed quick mitigation: 1) add a small per-tenant slot reservation for long sequences (e.g., reserve 1/8 of batch slots for >=256 token inflight). 2) clamp kernel selector to avoid mid-seq recompile unless seq length delta > 2x. 3) KV prefetch on batch start for sequences that have high prior cache miss rates.
meera: For experimentation, let's A/B these: A) batch-age-priority alone B) reserved-slots alone C) prefetched-KV + clamp selector. Run for 12 hours per rollout. Sam, can runtime sidecar toggle the 'reserved_slots' flag per pool?
sam_s: yes we can gate via feature flag and annotate pools. I'll scaffold flags + metrics (slot_util, reclaimed_tokens, kernel_switch_rate).
jin: One more idea: give long sequences 'soft affinity' to a GPU/worker core to improve KV locality — not full pin, but probabilistic routing so their subsequent chunks hit same cache. cheaper than full reservation.
katie: Add regression guard: if p99_long increases > 1.5x from baseline during rollout, auto rollback. ops-bot: deploy job 1901234689 started by sam_s (flags: reserved_slots=false, batch_age_priority=false). :gear:
alex_m: Perfect. After initial run I'll dump a detailed flamegraph. TLDR: cause = kernel churn + batching bias toward short requests => KV eviction + queue starvation for long sequences. Plan = try reservation/age-priority/affinity + conservative kernel clamp.
meera: Sounds good. I'll own metric tracking. ping me when first rollout completes. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy job 1901234802 completed (flags toggled: batch_age_priority=true)
alex_m: Early result after 2 hours: p99_long dropped ~28% with batch_age_priority but throughput for shorts slightly increased CPU jitter. Saving logs to /var/logs/rt/1901234567-run1.log and will attach flamegraphs shortly.
katie: Great. keep notes in the perf doc; we'll synthesize for postmortem if we need a rollback.
